chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ra'ab, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The believer is the brother of the believer, like one single body. If one part of it complains, the pain of that is felt in the rest of its body; and their spirits are from one spirit, and indeed the spirit of the believer is more intensely connected to the Spirit of Allah than the connection of the rays of the sun to it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of the bond between believers in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Abu Basir, highlighting the metaphysical unity of believers through the concept of 'Ruh al-Mu'min' (the believer's spirit). The hadith extends the well-known bodily analogy to emphasize that the believer's spirit is not only interconnected with others but shares a direct, intense connection with the Divine Spirit, surpassing even the physical proximity of sunlight to the sun. This underscores the Shia understanding of spiritual solidarity as a reflection of divine proximity.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, and a number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali Bin Raib, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘A Momin is a brother of a Momin, like one body. If there is a complaint of something from it, the pain of that is felt in the rest of his body; and their spirits are from one spirit, and that the spirit of the Momin is more intensely linked with the Spirit of Allahazwj than the linking of the rays of the sun with it’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa and A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad all from ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri’ab from abu Basir who has said the following:

“I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) say, ‘The believer is the brother (in belief) of the believer. They are like the same body. If one part complains of pain the rest of the body also feels it. Their spirits are from one spirit. The spirit of the believer’s connection with the spirit of Allah is stronger than the connection of the sun’s rays to the sun.’”
